page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6t.2xlarge is an instance type belonging to the enhanced compute-optimized ecs.c6t server family. Built on KVM virtualization, it features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated 8 vCPU Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The server contains 16.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This low memory-to-vCPU ratio aligns directly with compute-heavy instance configurations.

This instance configuration does not include local disk storage, requiring attached remote block storage solutions for persistent data needs. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processor capacity without thread contention from co-located virtual machines. However, the modest 16 GB RAM allocation limits compute-bound workloads that require larger in-memory footprints.

The compute-heavy configuration delivers cost efficiency for application architectures requiring sustained processing power over high memory capacity. Suitable deployment targets include web application servers, continuous integration build nodes, distributed compute tasks, batch processing scripts, and microservice backends that fit within a 16 GB memory boundary.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6t.2xlarge is an enhanced compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz across 8 vCPUs, it features 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance provides a baseline network speed of 3 Gbps and operates without bundled local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage volumes for persistent data management. With dedicated processing cores and a high CPU-to-memory ratio, the instance provides reliable performance for CPU-intensive tasks where massive memory overhead is unnecessary. It offers strong resource density for stateless application servers, build compilation pipelines, batch processing engines, and microservices workloads.
